name: Pirramimma Petit Verdot Ironstone 2013
text:
## Pirramimma Petit Verdot Ironstone 2013

**The story.** Pirramimma was founded in 1892 by Alexander Campbell Johnston and has been owned and run by his family ever since. The Johnstons settled in South Australia in 1839; Alexander, the tenth of thirteen children, bought 97 hectares of rich farmland just south-east of the young village of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Pirramimma,+McLaren+Vale,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k) and named it Pirramimma ([Trialto, the BC importer](https://trialto.kork.ca/fr/nos-domaines/pirramimma/petit-verdot-ironstone/2013), in French).

**The wine.** Pirramimma has long championed [Petit Verdot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petit_Verdot), a late-ripening Bordeaux grape usually used in small amounts in blends; James Halliday calls it "largely a workhorse and back-blending agent", and another critic quoted by the importer notes that it "used to ripen in Bordeaux once a decade" but ripens easily in McLaren Vale ([Trialto](https://trialto.kork.ca/fr/nos-domaines/pirramimma/petit-verdot-ironstone/2013)). The Ironstone is a varietal Petit Verdot.

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) calls 2013 "the hottest summer ever" for south-eastern Australia; yields were well down, but the vines proved fairly resistant to the record heat, with many varieties ripening unusually fast.

**What the critics say for 2013.**
- **[James Halliday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Halliday_%28writer%29): 95** (October 2016, via [Trialto](https://trialto.kork.ca/en/press-reviews/james-halliday-australian-wine-companion-petit-verdot-ironstone-2013)). "Hulking red with dry tannin ricocheting to all corners of the mouth, (thankfully) backed by a substantial volume of both curranty fruit and toasty/coffeed oak. The epitome of the 'cellaring style'. It needs to be left alone for some years."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.3** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is thirteen years old, the long rest Halliday asked for. The tannins should have softened, leaving currant, coffee, licorice and earth. Decant two hours ahead.

**Food.** Big flavours: braised beef cheeks, lamb shanks, or hard aged cheddar.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists it, but Trialto, the BC importer, can arrange case orders through a local store ([Trialto](https://trialto.kork.ca/en/press-reviews/james-halliday-australian-wine-companion-petit-verdot-ironstone-2013)).
